Maladaptive Strategies.value: push away positive emotions because they feel unsafe

Threat.value: I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day
I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger

Memory.value: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

issues.item: Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Perpetrator Cues' is hard to reconcile with the validated trauma type of toxic chemical exposure, which typically does not involve a discrete identifiable perpetrator. A clinician would question whether 'the person who harmed me' fits this trauma narrative.

issues.item: Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Emotionless Recall' and 'Rage on Recall' pull in opposing directions as dominant immediate recall states. Numbing/detached recall can coexist at times with anger, but presented together as parallel core memory qualities without any integrating context makes the node internally inconsistent.

issues.item: Rage on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense rage
issues.explanation: For toxic chemical exposure in this 76-year-old patient, the memory profile is otherwise dominated by fear/terror and vivid reliving. 'Rage on Recall' is not impossible, but here it sits in tension with the rest of the profile because there are no corresponding threat, appraisal, trigger, or strategy items reflecting anger/blame/resentment. The selected nodes instead describe a fear-based formulation (terror, danger scanning, night vigilance, sleep disturbance, avoidance of medical cues/care). This makes the anger item the only affective theme without supporting material, reducing internal coherence.
